verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a potential relationship between natalizumab and the High affinity immunoglobulin gamma Fc receptor I, mediated through the Low affinity immunoglobulin gamma Fc region receptor III-B. This is supported by the fact that natalizumab targets the Low affinity receptor III-B, which in turn is a target of both midostaurin and cetuximab, both of which also target the High affinity receptor I. The shared targeting of the Low affinity receptor III-B by natalizumab and other drugs indicates a possible mechanism of action involving the interaction with the Fc region of immunoglobulins. The evidence suggests that natalizumab may act by modulating the Fc receptor I, though the exact mechanism of this interaction remains to be fully elucidated. The presence of multiple pathways converging on the Low affinity receptor III-B supports the idea that natalizumab could influence the Fc receptor I through this intermediate step.
